subject: AuroraCode late-stage sizing: provisional capacity readout and next steps
messages:
From: Devon Meyer <devon@auroracode.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: AuroraCode capacity ask for late-stage POC

Karthik / team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We got internal thumbs-up to move the POC to a 3-week late-stage run to validate latency under our load and the larger context embedding pipeline. High level ask: can Redwood provision sustained capacity for the POC window (estimated 6,000 tokens/s peak across 6 concurrent workers) and keep that capacity isolated for the run?

Key constraints we shared in the call:
- Model: open-llama variant (approx. 30B); performance estimate assumes 32GB accelerator class (A100/compatible)
- Run window target: 2025-07-14 to 2025-08-04 (flexible by +/- 3 days)
- Expected sustained concurrency: 6 workers, average seq length 1,200
- Data residency: us-west region

Share any blocks or lead time required to put a provisional earmark on capacity. Also please confirm cost estimate ballpark so procurement can prep. I attached our POC requirements spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Devon Meyer
Head of Engineering, AuroraCode
devon@auroracode.ai

--- attachment: auroracode_mvp_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet) ---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Meyer <devon@auroracode.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: AuroraCode capacity ask for late-stage POC

Ben / Laura — forwarding AuroraCode's requirements. They want a 3-week late-stage POC with sustained capacity. Two asks from my side:
1) Quick inventory: what nodes/pools could satisfy a 6-worker sustained run with 30B model profile?
2) Can we tentatively earmark capacity for the 2025-07-14 start window (soft hold for ~21 days) and what lead time / cancellation terms apply?

I've attached the runbook they shared and flagged sequence lengths. Devon, included Ben and Laura to scope ops and pricing.

Karthik Iyer
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

--- attachment: Aurora_runbook_v2.pdf (pdf) ---

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: AuroraCode capacity ask for late-stage POC

Karthik — quick ops readout below. Short version: we have capacity to cover the POC but it requires a provisional earmark and a small configuration change. Details: 

Availability matrix (us-west pool snapshot):
- Node class: 32GB A100-equivalent GPUs
- Free nodes (unallocated): 18 GPUs
- Fragmentation note: 4 GPUs tied up in long-running dedicated pools (eligible to reshuffle with notice)
- Suitable contiguous allocation for 6 workers (each needs 1 GPU with room for kv cache) => 6 GPUs contiguous available
- If Aurora wants redundancy/throughput headroom (recommended) => 8 GPUs recommended to cover spikes and failover

Operational constraints and lead time:
- Provisional earmark: we can place a soft-hold for up to 30 days with no upfront payment; requires explicit start and end windows and a cancellation notice of 7 days
- Hard reserve: requires commit (monthly billing) and 14 days lead time for pool reconfiguration

Model/config notes:
- For 30B open-llama variant: target config is 32GB nodes, q4f16 quantization recommended for throughput; we should run pre-PoC microbench to validate token/s expectations
- KV cache warm-up: expect warm-up traffic for first 12 hours of the window; recommend enabling prefix caching for their session tokens to reduce per-token cost after warm-up

Attachments: capacity_snapshot_20250627.csv (pool-level counts)

Proposed next steps:
1) Place a provisional earmark of 8 GPUs in us-west for 2025-07-14 to 2025-08-04 (soft-hold) — I can file this today if Karthik / Devon confirm
2) Schedule a 60-minute microbench on one node with their model binary (Devon, we need a small container image or model artifact)
3) Send procurement a draft pricing placeholder (I can provide a ballpark POC rate + optional hard reserve pricing)

Ben Carter
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

--- attachment: capacity_snapshot_20250627.csv (csv) ---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Devon Meyer <devon@auroracode.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, AuroraCode Procurement <procurement@auroracode.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Jun 2025 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraCode capacity ask for late-stage POC

Devon — thanks, that's great news. Per Ben's readout we can place a provisional soft-hold for 8 GPUs in us-west for your requested window (2025-07-14 to 2025-08-04). A few quick items to confirm so we can lock the earmark: 

1) Can you confirm the model artifact/container by EOD Mon 2025-06-30 so Ben's team can run the microbench? If you prefer, we can run with the public artifact and you send a final container later.
2) Are you okay with the soft-hold terms (no upfront, 7-day cancellation notice)? Procurement, please confirm if you need a pro forma cost estimate now — Ben will provide a POC rate and hard-reserve pricing side-by-side.

Next steps:
- Ben will file the provisional hold when I confirm (today).
- We will schedule the microbench for 2025-07-01 or 2025-07-02 depending on the artifact availability.
- I'll open a HubSpot record and share a DocuSign placeholder for the POC terms.

Devon — once you confirm artifact timing I'll trigger the hold.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
